title: Spread coordinates on a two-page spread
concept: Page items are placed in spread coordinates: the spine is x = 0 and, as InDesign writes its own files, the pages' vertical centre is y = 0. Each Page is placed in that space by its own ItemTransform.

annotations.note: PageCount and BindingLocation describe the spread: two pages, with the spine after the first. The spread's own ItemTransform places it on the pasteboard.
The left page. Its bounds are 0 0 841.89 595.276 in its own space; its ItemTransform moves that rectangle to x = -595.276 … 0 and y = -420.945 … 420.945, so its right edge is the spine.
The right page starts at the spine (x = 0) and is shifted up by half its height, like the left page.
A frame on the left page. Its ItemTransform is in spread coordinates, so x is negative and y is measured from the vertical centre: -275.12 is 145.82 pt below the page's top edge.
The frame on the right page: x = 57.638 from the spine, the same y as its partner.
